title: Object: both sides — whole Word, yet grace-promises principal (Stapleton/Trent)
source_text: LV. Circa fidei objectum patet ex antedictis Reformatos Ecclesiae Romanae concedere omnia in universum quae Dei Verbo continentur ad fidei justificantis objectum pertinere; adeoque frustra Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae cum Reformatis disputant, quasi fidei objectum ad solas promissiones gratiae restringerent. Vicissim vero Theologi Ecclesiae Romanae, licet contendant fidei justificantis objectum tam late patere quam patet Dei Verbum, non negant tamen fidem justificantem circa promissiones Evangelicas potissimum versari, quemadmodum ex ipso Concilio Tridentino Thomas Stapletonus supra deduxit & probavit: ita ut nulla videatur hactenus ea de re esse controversia, quandoquidem utrique concedunt promissiones gratiae esse praecipuum fidei objectum, & tamen objectum fidei ad promissiones illas non esse restringendum.
pass_a_gloss: Concerning the object of faith it is clear from what was said before that the Reformed concede to the Roman Church that all things universally contained in God Word belong to the object of justifying faith; and so the Doctors of the Roman Church dispute with the Reformed in vain as if they restricted the object of faith to the promises of grace alone. Conversely the theologians of the Roman Church, although they contend that the object of justifying faith extends as widely as God Word extends, yet do not deny that justifying faith especially turns about the Gospel promises, as Thomas Stapleton above deduced and proved from the Council of Trent itself: so that there seems thus far to be no controversy on this matter, since both sides concede that the promises of grace are the principal object of faith, and yet that the object of faith is not to be restricted to those promises.
pass_b_english: Reformed grant Rome that justifying faith object covers all God Word contains; Rome wrongly charges a promises-only restriction.
Rome likewise grants Gospel promises as principal (Stapleton from Trent) while refusing restriction to promises alone — so little controversy remains here.
